subject: Synthesized exec snapshot — sprint outputs, near-term hazards, and concrete asks
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Synthesized exec snapshot — sprint outputs, near-term hazards, and concrete asks

Team —

Quick top-line snapshot to prep leadership for next week's QBR working session. This is intentionally concise: three sprint outputs, three near-term hazards, and three concrete asks for exec action or visibility. I attached the one-pager and a couple charts.

SPRINT OUTPUTS (what moved the needle)
- Serving latency: roll-forward of kernel patch reduced median token latency by ~9% on p3-small for seq<=512. Data in attachment: SLO_latency_chart.png
- Model catalog: validated 3 model variants (standard / quantized / fallback) for our LP use-case; can toggle routing per-customer tomorrow without infra changes.
- Billing projection: early batching+cache changes project 12% unit-cost reduction for hosted workloads (see billing_projection.xlsx).

NEAR-TERM HAZARDS / RISKS
- Capacity spikes: one Dedicated customer (Acme Corp) will onboard a new pipeline on 5/25; if dedicated pool autoscale isn't tuned we risk throttling and SLA breach. (Acme point: Jane Patel)
- Regression risk: the kernel patch relies on a new kernel path that hasn't seen long-tail traffic; telemetry shows a small uptick in 502s on rare long-context sessions.
- Sales / procurement friction: our current SOW timeline conflicts with Acme's procurement window — procurement needs a clearer mutual action plan.

CONCRETE ASKS (please action or note)
- Jonas: validate dedicated autoscale policy for Acme by EOD Wed 5/19; propose safe burst cap and rollback plan.
- Laura: confirm we can approve a 60-day SLA exception if we need to delay full Dedicated capacity for Acme; if not, advise alternate mitigation.
- Karthik / Marissa: prep a succinct mutual action plan (MAP) for Acme that ties tech milestones to procurement checkpoints; share draft before Fri 5/21.

ATTACHMENTS:
- QBR_onepager_v2.pdf (one-pager for exec)
- SLO_latency_chart.png (median/P95 token-lat charts)
- billing_projection.xlsx (cost model: baseline vs. batching+cache)

I'll be in the working session Monday and can run the first slide. If you need a short pre-read call, I'm available 10–11am PST today.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesized exec snapshot — sprint outputs, near-term hazards, and concrete asks

Thanks Hannah —

I can take the autoscale validation. Quick clarifying question: for the Acme onboarding, are they planning sustained throughput or spiky batch windows? That changes the safe burst cap.

I'll run a short load profile test today against a mirrored workload and report recommended autoscale params by 5/19 EOD.

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 May 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Synthesized exec snapshot — sprint outputs, near-term hazards, and concrete asks

Appreciate the concise format, Hannah — this is helpful. Two quick notes: 

1) SLA exception: I can greenlight a time-limited 60-day exception for Acme, provided we have a clear mitigation and rollback path owned by infra. Jonas, please include explicit rollback steps in your autoscale validation so product + sales can accept the exception.

2) MAP draft: Marissa / Karthik, please include a single-line procurement milestone (legal signoff target + expected doc circulation dates) — we need that to coordinate with Acme's procurement and our finance team. If you can share a draft MAP by Thursday 5/20 COB I will review before the QBR.

Also agree we should add a backup plan slide to the QBR one-pager with a short-run timeline: immediate (0–7d), short (7–30d), and medium (30–90d). Hannah — can you update the one-pager to include this backup plan? Small ask.

On the regression: Jonas, prioritize tracing for those long-context sessions and add a canary rollout plan we can revert in <15 minutes.

Thanks all — Laura
Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff, Operations
Redwood Inference

Forwarded attachment stub: QBR_onepager_v2.pdf (updated request: add backup plan slide)
